title: Adic formal smoothness gives lifts into complete rings along closed ideals
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$ an ideal such that $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Let $A$ be a commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and $J\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $J^t\subseteq I$ for some $t\ge1$ and $J=\bigcap_{m\ge1}(J+I^m)$ ($J$ is closed for the $I$-adic topology). Let $q:A\to A/J$ be the quotient map, with $A/J$ an $R$-algebra via $q$, and let $g:S\to A/J$ be a homomorphism of $R$-algebras such that $g(\mathfrak n^r)\subseteq q(I)$ for some $r\ge1$. Then there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:S\to A$ with $q\circ f=g$, and $f(\mathfrak n^{rt})\subseteq I$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous, line 9257) and its proof, for $R$ with the discrete topology (Definition Tag 07NI, definition-formally-smooth-adic, line 9213, condition (2)(b)); 'A adic' is Definition Tag 07E8 (definition-topological-ring, line 8959) (8): pre-adic with ideal of definition I and complete, i.e. A -> lim A/I^n bijective; continuity of g for the I-adic quotient topology on A/J is, by Lemma Tag 07E9 (lemma-continuous), g(n^r) in (I+J)/J for some r
